name: merger-agreement
description: Extract key deal points from an M&A merger agreement. Mirrors Harvey's published Merger Agreements workflow (27 fields, 99.66% recall floor on matched corpus).

columns.description: All named parties to the merger (acquirer, target, subsidiaries).
Execution date of the agreement (ISO 8601).
Expected closing date if stated (ISO 8601).
Structure of the transaction: merger, stock purchase, asset purchase, reverse merger, etc.
Total consideration. Return amount + currency.
Mix of cash, stock, earnout, assumed liabilities.
Stock exchange ratio or cash-per-share if stated.
US state whose law governs the agreement.
Forum / venue for disputes.
Whether the agreement contains a no-solicit / no-shop provision.
If no_solicit_clause is true, the verbatim scope text.
Break-up fee (termination fee payable on acceptance of superior proposal).
Reverse break-up fee (fee payable by acquirer on regulatory/financing failure).
Required regulatory approvals (HSR, CFIUS, foreign antitrust, sector regulators).
Verbatim MAE / MAC clause definition.
Named carve-outs from the MAE definition.
Survival period for representations and warranties.
Indemnification cap / limitation of liability if stated.
Indemnification deductible / basket.
Escrow amount for indemnification / working capital.
Key conditions precedent to closing beyond standard ones.
Whether the acquirer's obligation is conditioned on financing.
Treatment of target employees / equity awards (brief summary).
Whether the agreement includes non-compete provisions for key executives.
Duration of non-compete if present.
Survival period for confidentiality obligations.
Mechanism for disputes: litigation, arbitration (incl. rules), mediation.

notes: Use provenance='cited' so every extracted value cites a verbatim source span.
MAE / MAC clauses are often multi-paragraph; verbatim_quote columns emit the full clause.
Termination fees are usually explicit dollar amounts; reverse termination fees may be structured as percentages of deal value.
Regulatory approvals often hide in the 'Efforts' covenant; scan for HSR Act, CFIUS, foreign antitrust.
